reference.title: The screens of the app
reference.shortdesc: What each item in the menu shows, what the top of every screen holds, and a picture of the main screens.

section.title: The tree in the pages that follow
section.p: The pages of this chapter use the sample tree, the Brontë family of Haworth. To open it, choose in the menu, then choose on the card of the sample. If you removed it, make the people in the pages by hand. shows how.

section.title: The menu
section.p: The menu stays at the left of every screen. Some items show your whole tree. Others show one person. That person is named in the chip that starts with .

table.title: The menu items and what they show

row.entry: The name of your tree, how much it holds, and a search box.
The page of one person, with their family tree beside it.
A drawing of the person with parents, partners and children.
The things that happened in that person's life.
Your family trees, one card for each.
Your own notes about that person.
The archives, libraries and websites your sources come from.
The people credited with the tree.
Your list of questions and ideas.
The colours and the light or dark look.
The version of the app and facts about your computer.

section.note: If a page has no person to show, it needs one first. Search for someone, then open them. shows how.

section.title: The top of every screen
section.p: These stay in the same places as you move around.

ul.li: The name of your tree, then a trail of the pages you came through, such as Home and then People. Choose a name in the trail to go back to it.
A back arrow, on a page you opened from another page. Choose it to go back one step.
The chip that starts with . It names the person, or the family, that the menu pages are about.
The button. It opens the sheet.

section.p: Home shows the name of your tree and a line that counts its people, families and events. Under it are a search box, the button and a button with a small icon and no words. The icon opens a panel with the heading . shows how to search.
Two more buttons sit under the search box. lists everyone in the tree. goes to your list of trees.
After you have opened a person, Home has two more headings. Under is a button with the name of the person you opened last. Under is a button for each person you opened lately.
A tree with nobody in it shows instead.

This is the list that opens. It has one card for each person. A card shows the name, the years of life and small chips. One chip counts the sources and one counts the events. starts a new person: shows how.
Each card is one family tree. It tells you how many people, families and events the tree holds. The tree you have open has the mark. and start here.
This is one person's page. It has parts for (the names and the sex), , , , and . Each part with facts has a chip that counts its sources.

A line above the names says how the person was added. The buttons , , and are at the foot of the page. When the window is wide enough, the family tree of the person shows beside the page. explains the tree.

Notes are your own written words about a person, kept with their record. shows how to write one.
These three pages list things that belong to the whole tree. You add to each with .

ul.li: lists the archives, libraries, websites and family collections that hold your sources.
lists the people or groups credited with the tree.
is your research log: questions, ideas and things to do. Each has a status.
